question: Does the production AsyncGRPO scoring output, after a policy-version transition causes per-sample queue filtering, reach the production rollout collator as a partial same-group training batch?

estimand.primary: Number of active completion tokens from one scored prompt group that the production DataCollatorForRollout receives after queue staleness filtering.
estimand.secondary: Fraction of the full group's active completion tokens retained after one policy-version transition.
estimand.claim_boundary: This measures the training batch handed to the real collator; it does not execute compute_loss or an optimizer step and does not measure downstream task success.

method.scoring: Invoke the source's real _AsyncRolloutLoop._score_group on one three-completion RolloutGroup with one TrainingSequence per completion, fixed rewards [0,1,2], one common group_id, and model_version 0.
method.queue_and_packing: Pass the scorer's RolloutSample outputs through real RolloutQueueDataset.__iter__, advance callback-visible current version from 0 to 1 after reading the first row with max_staleness=0, then pass the surviving rows to real DataCollatorForRollout.torch_call.
method.control: Run the same scored outputs through the queue with current version held at 0 and verify all three rows and three active completion tokens reach the collator.

failure_criteria: Pinned source revision or file hashes differ.
Scoring does not emit the frozen three-row group.
The fixed-version control does not preserve all rows/tokens.
The version-transition arm does not deliver the frozen partial batch to the production collator.
A GPU, model download, paid API, or external service is required.
